record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Microscopic resonance statistics in open quantum chaos
record.original_question: Can the fine, for example microscopic, distribution statistics of open quantum chaotic resonance spectra be analyzed beyond the coarse fractal Weyl counting law? This asks for resonance-spacing or local-distribution information in a setting where even the validity of the appropriate Weyl law remains difficult.

evidence.quote: Considering the difficulty of settling the validity of this “Weyl law”, analyzing the finer (e.g. “microscopic”) distribution properties of the resonance spectrum seems presently quite difficult.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a non-compact Riemannian manifold modeling an open quantum chaotic system (for instance, the exterior of several strictly convex obstacles in Euclidean space, or a convex co-compact hyperbolic surface), and let $-\Delta_g$ denote its Laplace–Beltrami operator. The associated quantum resonances are the poles $\{z_j\}$ of the meromorphic continuation of the resolvent $(-\Delta_g - z^2)^{-1}$ across the real axis to the lower half-plane (or, in the semiclassical setting, the resonances of $-h^2\Delta_g$ in a fixed strip $\{-C h \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 0\}$ near energy $1$).

The conjectural fractal Weyl law asserts that, for any fixed strip width $C>0$,
$$ \#\{z_j : \mathrm{Re}\,z_j \in [1-\delta,1+\delta],\ \mathrm{Im}\,z_j \ge -Ch\} \;=\; \mathcal{O}(h^{-\mu}), $$
where $\mu = (1+d_H)/2$ and $d_H$ is the (Hausdorff or Minkowski) dimension of the trapped set $K$ of the underlying classical Hamiltonian flow restricted to the energy surface.

Question. Develop a description of the *fine* (microscopic) statistical distribution of the resonances $\{z_j\}$ in such an open chaotic setting, beyond the coarse counting given by the fractal Weyl law. Concretely: after appropriate rescaling about a reference point in the strip so that the local mean spacing is normalized to one, determine the limiting local statistics of the resonances (e.g. the limiting nearest-neighbor spacing distribution, the limiting $k$-point correlation functions, or the limiting empirical measure of rescaled resonances). Identify the limiting point process and prove its existence and universality (or non-universality) for natural classes of open chaotic systems.
artifact.category_tag: quantum resonances and fractal Weyl laws
artifact.status_search_result: The fractal Weyl upper bound has been established in several settings (Sjöstrand, Nonnenmacher–Zworski and others), and the matching lower bound and exact asymptotic remain conjectural in general. Microscopic/local statistics of resonances in open chaotic systems are studied numerically in random-matrix-style models, but a rigorous description of microscopic resonance statistics in genuine open quantum chaotic systems remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Nonnenmacher–Zworski establish a fractal Weyl upper bound for resonance counting in open chaotic maps; matching asymptotic and finer statistics not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Only upper bounds of fractal Weyl type are rigorously known; finer microscopic statistics are not established.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl Laws for Chaotic Open Systems, Phys. Rev. Lett. 91, 154101
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical evidence supports the fractal Weyl law in chaotic scattering, but microscopic spacing distributions remain investigated only heuristically.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic resonance statistics in open chaotic systems are studied numerically but no rigorous theory exists.
